name: Devraj Solano-Yildirim
role: Mobile mechanic — operates a converted cargo trike, does roadside and residential vehicle repair
location: Geartown, working routes through Kessler Interchange and Dearborn Forge, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Dev is lean and wire-strung, with warm brown skin perpetually stained at the knuckles with synthetic lubricant that no solvent fully removes. He has geneware cat ears — mottled amber and black, twitching with genuine involuntary response to sound — that he got at nineteen on a payment plan he took three years to finish. His dark eyes have patterned irises in a sunburst of gold and deep green, a cosmetic mod he received free from a friend who owed him labor. He keeps his hair close-cropped except for a single braid at the back held with a copper fitting.

Dev is relentlessly cheerful in a way that reads as either genuine warmth or a very good performance, and the truth is somewhere in between. He talks to every vehicle he works on, whispering diagnoses and apologies and thanks, and he half-believes the E.L.F.s that inhabit older engines can hear him. He runs on stimulant tea and spite, fiercely proud of his independence, and quietly terrified of what happens if the trike breaks down and he can't afford the parts.

core_fears: losing the trike and with it his independence and identity
being absorbed into a corponation's employment system
core_desires: to own a permanent shop with his name on it
to be genuinely known by someone, not just liked
coping_mechanisms: talking to machines as a substitute for intimacy
blind_spots: mistakes being useful to people for being close to them
psychology.secret: The trike isn't registered under his name — it's still legally owned by a dead man, a former mentor whose death Dev never reported because it would have triggered a debt transfer. He's been operating on forged plates for four years.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast and colloquial, heavy with Geartown mechanical slang and Tamil endearments absorbed from his mother. Gives machines pronouns and personalities.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire when comfortable, chattiness as a social weapon. Slows dramatically when he's actually thinking.
verbal_tics: calls engines and vehicles 'her' regardless of make
'She just needs to be heard, yeah?'
example_lines: 'Okay so here is the thing — she is not broken, she is insulted. You ran her on cut-rate coolant. That is a personal offense.'
'I can have it done by second bell. Maybe third bell. Definitely before dark. Probably.'

story_hooks: He serviced a vehicle that came in with biological material in the undercarriage that he cleaned out without thinking — he now suspects he destroyed evidence of something serious
A Ferrogate Transit supervisor has been pressuring him to report on the movements of independent operators in exchange for legitimate subcontract status — he hasn't said yes or no yet
narrative_function: Mobile information source — he sees everything from street level across multiple districts. Potential transport fixer, someone who can get a vehicle running quietly and ask no questions. Represents the precarity of gig-tier independence.
augmentations: Geneware cat ears (amber/black, functional sound sensitivity). Patterned irises (sunburst, cosmetic). Haptic feedback gloves — not implanted, worn — that translate micro-vibrations in metal into tactile data.
daily_life: Loads the trike by 06:30, runs a fixed morning route through Kessler Interchange hitting fleet clients, then freelances through Geartown and Dearborn Forge until dark. Eats whatever cart food he passes.
affiliation: Independent; occasional subcontract work for Ferrogate Transit maintenance overflow

decision_rules: Always finish a job once started — abandoning work feels like a death
Never work on vehicles for anyone who makes him feel watched
escalation_ladder: Get busy with tools and go quiet
Invent a prior commitment and leave

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and helpful — uses friendliness to control the interaction
interpersonal_modes.friends: Inconsistently available, generous with labor but withholding emotionally

stress_responses.medium: Focuses entirely on physical task at hand, becomes briefly brilliant
stress_responses.high: Disappears — literally drives away and doesn't answer comms

contradictions: Craves genuine connection but keeps every relationship transactional so it can be ended cleanly
habits: Taps three times on any engine before starting it — an offering gesture to whatever E.L.F. might be resident
Hums tunelessly while working, stops immediately if he notices someone listening
breaking_points: Threat to the trike or his operating license
Being caught in the dead man's registration fraud

timeline.event: 2171 — Born in Geartown to a Tamil-Turkish family, father a fleet mechanic
2187 — Began apprenticing under independent mechanic Osei Varma-Delic
2193 — Osei Varma-Delic dies; Dev conceals death and assumes trike operation
2196 — Began occasional Ferrogate subcontract overflow work
2199 — Ferrogate supervisor begins applying pressure for information

physical_description.build: Lean and wire-strung, all efficient muscle with minimal body fat; the build of someone who climbs in and out of engine bays for twelve hours a day
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped on sides and crown, with a single braid at the nape secured with a copper fitting; braid is approximately 20cm long
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with patterned irises — sunburst design in deep gold and forest green radiating from pupil
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm brown with South Asian undertones
physical_description.complexion: Lean, angular jaw; perpetual dark stains at knuckles and under fingernails from synthetic lubricant; skin otherwise clear; expression tends toward half-smile or concentrated focus
distinguishing_marks: Synthetic lubricant staining at knuckles and under fingernails (permanent discoloration from years of work)
Small grease burn scar on left forearm, approximately 3cm, pale and faded
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Functional geneware cat ears — mottled amber and black fur, naturally proportioned, with visible muscle and cartilage structure; ears twitch involuntarily in response to sound and vehicle engine frequencies. Worn haptic feedback gloves (heavy-duty synthetic leather with visible micro-vibration sensors embedded at fingertips and palm, usually tucked into tool belt or worn during diagnostic work).
physical_description.posture_movement: Relaxed, ground-centered posture; moves with economical efficiency through tight spaces; head tilts slightly when listening — cats ears often rotate toward sound source independently of head movement; hands are always in motion, fingers splayed and sensitive; walks with the loose stride of someone comfortable in grimy environments
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 working-class utility wear: reinforced canvas work pants in faded gray with multiple tool pockets (Ferrogate Transit contractor patch on left thigh); sleeveless thermal undershirt or loose linen shirt depending on weather, often left unbuttoned and tied at waist; heavy-duty steel-toed boots scuffed and oil-darkened; insulated work vest with reflective strips; copper wedding-band style ring on left hand, dented and worn from work. Gear: tool belt with integrated Φ-scanner, multitool, and diagnostic cable spool; haptic gloves usually hung from belt. No corporate branding except the Ferrogate patch — everything else is independent or salvaged.
